title: Final Report on the Capsizing on 28 September 1994 in the Baltic Sea of the Ro-Ro Passenger Vessel MV ESTONIA
author: Joint Accident Investigation Commission of Estonia, Finland and Sweden (JAIC)
notes: The original official investigation. Concluded the bow visor locks failed under wave loads, the visor tore off and pulled the bow ramp open, flooding the car deck. Chapter 21.3 reproduces survivor reports deck by deck.

title: Final Report of the Preliminary Assessment of MV ESTONIA
author: Estonian Safety Investigation Bureau (OJK), Swedish Accident Investigation Authority (SHK), Safety Investigation Authority Finland (OTKES)
notes: Concluded the ship sank due to failure of the bow structure; the starboard hull damage found in 2020 resulted from contact with the seabed; no need to reopen the safety investigation.

title: Preliminary assessment of new information on the sinking of the passenger ship M/V ESTONIA (interim reporting)
author: Swedish Accident Investigation Authority (SHK)
notes: Case page for the 2021–2025 re-examination, including wreck surveys and the bow ramp recovery.

title: Research study on the sinking sequence of MV Estonia (SSPA Sweden AB consortium and HSVA consortium)
author: SSPA / Chalmers / HSVA et al., commissioned by Swedish governmental agency VINNOVA
notes: Presented 5 May 2008. Found the sinking sequence followed the JAIC scenario in all essential respects, but that it began earlier than JAIC stated. Did not question the cause.

title: Investigation Report on the Capsizing of MV Estonia (German Group of Experts)
author: German Group of Experts (commissioned via the builder Meyer Werft)
notes: Disputed the JAIC report. Alleged poor maintenance, water regularly on the car deck, a non-compliant collision bulkhead extension, and claimed small explosions near the visor contributed. Rejected by Finnish experts and others.

title: Inquiry into Swedish Armed Forces transports on M/S Estonia (Hirschfeldt inquiry)
author: Johan Hirschfeldt, for the Swedish Government
notes: Confirmed non-explosive military electronic equipment was carried on 14 and 20 September 1994, but found no military shipment on the night of the sinking.

title: Estonian Government Expert Committee on the sinking of MS Estonia (Kurm commission)
author: Chaired by former state prosecutor Margus Kurm
notes: Criticised the JAIC report for lacking analysis of the bangs survivors reported and for not ruling out an explosion near the visor attachments. Kurm later publicly argued for a submarine-collision hypothesis, which is not supported by the 2025 official findings.

title: Agreement between the Republic of Estonia, the Republic of Finland and the Kingdom of Sweden regarding the M/S Estonia
author: Governments of Estonia, Finland and Sweden
notes: Designates the wreck and surrounding area as a final place of rest and criminalises disturbing it (the 'grave peace').

title: The Hole: Another Look at the Sinking of the Estonia Ferry on September 28th, 1994
author: Drew Wilson
notes: 406-page critical examination of alternative explanations (collision or explosion) set against post-Soviet smuggling in the Baltic.

title: Die Estonia: Tragödie eines Schiffsuntergangs
author: Jutta Rabe
notes: German journalist's account alleging a cover-up; basis of the feature film Baltic Storm (2003). Rabe co-organised the controversial 2000 dive with Gregg Bemis.

title: Estonia's Four Mysteries
author: The Estonia Group (lead article by Knut Carlqvist)
notes: Summarises the issues critics consider unresolved: the bangs, the visor, the speed of sinking and the official handling.

title: Estonia – fyndet som ändrar allt (Estonia: The Find That Changes Everything)
author: Henrik Evertsson (director), Discovery / Dplay
notes: ROV footage revealed previously unreported starboard hull damage (about 4 m high, up to 1.2 m wide). Triggered the 2021–2025 re-examination.

title: Filmmakers fined over exploring wreck of 1994 ferry disaster
author: Euronews
notes: Evertsson and Linus Andersson, first acquitted (German-flagged vessel), were convicted on retrial of disturbing the grave peace; the Court of Appeal later doubled the day-fines.

title: Photos: MS Estonia bow ramp raised
author: ERR News
notes: The 12-tonne bow ramp was lifted on 25 July 2023 from the research vessel Viking Reach and taken to Estonia via Paldiski.

title: Feature | MS Estonia disaster: Official version versus critique
author: ERR News
notes: Overview of the official account and its critics.

title: Sweden pays tribute to Estonia disaster victims
author: The Local Sweden
notes: Casualty figures: 501 Swedish and 285 Estonian dead; 94 bodies recovered.

title: Blog: Sara Hedrenius – surviving the MS Estonia disaster and the journey of resilience and recovery
author: International Maritime Rescue Federation
notes: First-person survivor account.

title: The Sinking of a Luxury Ferry and a Few Lessons on Survival
author: VICE
notes: Survivor interviews.

title: Sole Brit survivor of 'modern Titanic' disaster
author: Daily Post (Wales)
notes: Interview with Paul Barney, the only British survivor.

title: 830 likely dead in ferry accident
author: Associated Press via Deseret News
notes: Contemporary AP report including engineer Henrik Sillaste's statement.

title: Death in the Baltic: the MI6 connection
author: New Statesman
notes: Investigative feature on smuggling allegations; reports crew testimony including seaman Silver Linde.

title: Riksarkivet (Swedish National Archives) – Estonia collection
author: Riksarkivet
notes: Holds JAIC material, the 2008 research studies and photographic records.

title: Estonia investigator accused of destroying evidence
author: The Local Sweden
notes: Hirschfeldt reported to the Justice Ombudsman over destruction of background material from his inquiry.
